Neutral gray shark back and tall visible fin retain rear view; face and teeth stay hidden. Blonde hair, turquoise headband and splash placement retained.
Upright shark turns toward the mermaid with pointed snout, gills, ivory underside, sly half-lidded eye and triangular teeth. Mermaid rear view and bent hand preserved.

Rebuilt source anatomy: compact shark head sits above the nearly horizontal far pectoral fin gesturing to the right. Near fin hangs left and ends behind the waterline. One dorsal fin, neutral gray skin, gills, ivory underside and sly toothy grin. V2 had both fins down; v3 recovered gesture but added an extra forehead fin and below-water tip; v4 removes both defects.
Gray shark with a sly toothy grin. The forward right fin is separate from the normal jaw; the near fin hangs against the flank. Extra rear fin removed.
The shark leans up-right and raises the far pectoral fin. Normal compact face, triangular teeth, gray flank and pale belly edge follow the corrected shark identity.
Tall upright shark with raised forward fin and its blunt lifted tip. The toothy mouth stays above the fin; near fin hangs along the flank.
Forward fin angles moderately upward beneath the shark's sly toothy face. Near fin hangs down; extra rear fin removed.

Far pectoral fin reaches almost horizontally right with a slightly upturned tip. Normal shark jaw remains above it; extra rear fin removed. Review the mouth opening: this candidate has a narrower toothy grin than the original speaking pose.
Forward fin has the original drooping tip. Compact sneaky face and razor teeth replace the dolphin interpretation; extra rear fin removed.
Narrow forward fin arches downward, clearly separate from the normal toothy jaw. Gray body, pale belly edge, gills and sly eye match the corrected shark.
Both eyes are visible above the open toothy grin. Broad pale belly faces the viewer; the right fin bends outward and down while the near fin hangs low.
Both eyes look up-right above a mischievous open mouth. The left fin rises beside the head and the right fin extends outward; backward lean retained.
Gray shark with toothy smirk and outward pectoral fins retains the source interaction. Mermaid looks back left with one hand near collarbone and far arm dipping into water.
Gray shark keeps lowered near pectoral-fin gesture toward the mermaid's reaching human hand. Human arm and gray fin stay distinct; mermaid pose, gaze and flowing hair retained.

Two-eye three-quarter shark face now has sneaky brow and triangular teeth. Mermaid continues swimming right with one trailing arm; shark's separate far fin reaches toward that arm. V3 removes the duplicated back fin from v2, leaving one dorsal and two pectoral fins.
Upright gray shark watches the mermaid dip face-first toward the water. Her right-facing head, hair and sliver of swimsuit shoulder retained; no submerged body completed.

Replaced blue dolphin material with neutral gray and replaced friendly wide eyes with sly half-lidded eyes. Both eyes and the yellow hair remain visible. No teeth were added because the mouth is underwater.
Gray shark back and fin retain the shallow dive composition, cyan-white wave and separate yellow hair tuft. No face or additional anatomy introduced.
Neutral-gray shark dorsal fin retains its rightmost position and long leftward cyan-white wake. Source contains no face or teeth, and neither was added.
Neutral-gray swept shark fin above the thin cyan-white waterline. The smooth fin remains more curved than the blocky source outline, consistent with the preceding converted fin drawings.
